bio: Just a nerd building stuff, writing blogs, and trying (sometimes too hard) to be social. Thanks for visiting my website!

faq.question: What did you want to be when you grew up?
faq.answer: The short answer is to be happy. The long answer is finding out what makes me happy. At the moment, I think I do want to be some form of entrepreneur-ship in the next 5-10 years.

faq.question: What engages you outside of work?
faq.answer:
Side projects, especially automation related. If you pitch me a project, we would probably have a long conversation about it :)
Being a home chef. The dish I am most proud of is Vietnamese-style ginger chicken (close second is Steak).
Mentorship experience. I am involved in a variety of volunteering organizations to teach about software development and push for more technical context
All kind of games (video games, board games, sports even though I am bad at it, etc), pop cultures (anime, movies, tv series, etc)

faq.question: What are your quirks?
faq.answer: People told me that I can adapt to operate under any environment (I suspect this is the result of study abroad from early age).

faq.question: What might I misunderstand about you?
faq.answer: When solving problems or resolving blockers, I spent a lot of time to try to build a mental model. Sometimes during discussions, I would bring up information that might seems irrelevant and even drive us off the main topic.

faq.question: What's your relationship with Chime? Email? In-person?
faq.answer:
I think in-person would be the most effective for brainstorming and exploring the unknowns (and random/meander conversation)
Slack is my preferred method of communication. I have it on all my devices so I can response based on urgency and importance (Normally I would answer immediately if I know answer on top of my head). I think it is the easiest to start a conversation and it also acts as a note taker for you.
I still consider email as the most formal method of communication and generally I would spend more effort to draft any email out (which means it would take more time for me to response). I think this is effective when we need to create awareness for 1-to-many larger count of audience

faq.question: What is your work routine? (Work from home? Core hours? Focus blocks?)
faq.answer: My core hours are 10:00AM - 6:00PM but I generally start from 8:30AM - 6:30PM. My focus blocks usually jn the morning but can be adjusted. If I truly need focus, I would mark it on my calendar so if as long as you see an opening in my calendar, that means I am available.

faq.question: How should we handle interruptive questions? (How should I approach you for questions? - Chime, email, in person, ect.)
faq.answer:
Through Slack would be best because I can read the questions again multiple time to get the details and also for record.
Never hesitate to ask me questions. If I know the answer, I would give you all I know. If I don't know the answer, I will try to find someone who can or work with you to get closer to the answer (depends on time). Either way, we will learn something out of it.

faq.question: What team meetings do you have strong opinions about?
faq.answer: I like lunch & learns since crucial to better value.

faq.question: What qualities do you particularly value in people you work with?
faq.answer:
I value difference of opinion as I believe that is how we individually grow.
I value people with strong sense of mentorship and have the ability to build out framework/mechanism, regardless of their experience level
I value people with variety sense of humor

faq.question: What are you currently focusing on for your own growth?
How would you like your teammates to support you?
faq.answer: I think everyone is supportive as-is on my work. However, I would like to propose for every unknown/area/services, we should have a tag team of at least two (one main person and one shadow) on exploration/discussion meetings. I think it would allow more context within each team and we can avoid problems when we only have a one critical point of failure.

faq.question: What is your relationship with positive feedback? Constructive feedback?
faq.answer:
I think there is a high diminishing returns on positive feedback so there should be a balance.
I always welcome of constructive feedback at any time. If I don't receive them in a while, I will actively look out for it to make sure you have not given up on helping me improve.

faq.question: How do you prefer to receive feedback?
faq.answer: I would like to receive as soon as possible before I cause more of the same trouble. I will note whether it is from Slack, email, chime or in person
